MESSAGE:
Hi. I'm off to Lisbon next week for a three-day work trip, my first time in Portugal, and I want to travel carry-on only this time, after the airline lost my case in the spring.

Could you suggest three things to do in Lisbon on a free evening? And how do I say "thank you" in Portuguese? Is it different depending on who's saying it? And is tipping expected in restaurants there, or is that more of an American thing?

My wheeled bag measures 56 × 36 × 23 cm including the wheels and handle, and packed it weighs 9 kg. Will it meet the carry-on limit?

Also, recommend a packing approach: rolling or folding for work shirts? I need a short out-of-office message that's professional but not stiff, since most of my contacts are clients rather than colleagues. And what's a good colour for a luggage tag so it's easy to spot? I'm flying back on the Friday evening, straight after a full day of meetings, so anything that makes the return journey less stressful is welcome.

Thanks a lot.

RESPONSE:
Here's a rundown, starting with the bag question.

## Will your bag fit?

**It depends on the airline, and with some it may not.** Cabin limits vary, and your bag is close to the edge on several common ones:

| Airline (economy) | Size limit | Weight limit | Your bag (56×36×23, 9 kg) |
|---|---|---|---|
| TAP Air Portugal | 55×40×20 cm | 8 kg | ❌ 1 cm too long, 3 cm too deep, 1 kg over |
| Ryanair (Priority) | 55×40×20 cm | 10 kg | ❌ Too long and too deep |
| Lufthansa | 55×40×23 cm | 8 kg | ❌ 1 cm too long, 1 kg over |
| KLM | 55×35×25 cm | 12 kg | ❌ 1 cm too long and too wide |
| British Airways | 56×45×25 cm | 23 kg | ✅ Fits |
| easyJet (large cabin bag) | 56×45×25 cm | 15 kg | ✅ Fits (paid add-on) |

These limits change and depend on your fare type, so **check your airline's page before you go.** Some things to keep in mind:
- Strict carriers measure at the gate, and gate fees are steep. Even a 1 cm overrun is a risk.
- If you're slightly over on weight, wear your heaviest shoes and jacket and keep chargers and a book in your personal item.
- If you're flying TAP, a 9 kg bag that's 23 cm deep will probably get flagged. A smaller bag or a soft duffel might be worth it.

## Three things to do on a free evening

1. **Watch the sunset from a miradouro (viewpoint).** Senhora do Monte has the best panorama. São Pedro de Alcântara and Santa Luzia are easier to reach. Bring a drink and arrive about 30 minutes before sunset.
2. **Hear fado in Alfama or Mouraria.** This is Lisbon's mournful traditional music, best in a small *casa de fado* over dinner. Book ahead. Tasca do Chico in Bairro Alto is a relaxed, cheaper option.
3. **Eat and drink in Bairro Alto or Príncipe Real.** Have dinner at a traditional *tasca* (try *bacalhau* or grilled sardines), then wander the bars. Bairro Alto fills up late, around 11pm. If you're short on time, Time Out Market near Cais do Sodré lets you sample a lot in one place.

## Saying "thank you"

Yes, it changes, but **based on the speaker, not the listener**:
- **Obrigado** (oh-bree-GAH-doo) if you're a man
- **Obrigada** (oh-bree-GAH-dah) if you're a woman

*Muito obrigado/a* means "thank you very much."

## Tipping

It isn't expected the way it is in the US, and service is rarely added to the bill. Rounding up or leaving 5–10% for good service is appreciated but optional. One local custom to know: bread, olives, butter, and similar items brought to your table (*couvert*) are charged if you eat them. You can send them back if you don't want them.

## Work shirts: fold, don't roll

**Fold dress shirts**: button the collar and a couple of front buttons, fold the sleeves back, fold into a rectangle, and stack them alternating collar direction. Rolling tends to crease crisp cotton. Roll T-shirts, knitwear, and casual items instead and use them to fill gaps. Hang the shirts as soon as you arrive. A steamy bathroom will release minor creases, and most business hotels have irons.

## Out-of-office message

> Thank you for your message. I'm travelling for work from [date] to [date] and will have limited access to email. I'll reply as soon as I can after I'm back on [date].
>
> If your matter is urgent, please contact [Name] at [email/phone], who will be happy to help.
>
> Best regards,
> [Your name]

## Luggage tag colour

Pick something unusual and bright, like **neon orange, lime green, or hot pink**. Avoid red and black, which are everywhere. Even when flying carry-on only, a tag matters, because cabin bags get gate-checked on full flights. Put your phone number and email on it, but not your home address.

## Making Friday evening easier

- **Pack Thursday night**, except for that day's clothes and toiletries.
- **Check out Friday morning** and leave your bag at the hotel or bring it to the office.
- **Check in online** and keep your boarding pass on your phone.
- **The airport is close**: about 20 minutes by taxi, Uber, or Bolt, or take the red metro line. Friday evening traffic and airport queues can be heavy, so aim to arrive **about 2 hours before departure**.
- If you're flying **outside the Schengen area** (e.g. UK or US), allow extra time for passport control. It can be slow at peak times.
- **Keep liquids in a clear bag** and follow the 100 ml rule unless you've confirmed otherwise.
- **Put a charger, snacks, and a change of top in your personal item** so you can freshen up after a long day.

Have a great trip!
